subject: How to speed up my stan code.

messages.author: 39f92c300d8c81a9
messages.subject: How to speed up my stan code.
parts:
Hello
I want to know how can I speeding up my code.
I tried ADVI, but it takes long time.

This is my stan code.
data {
  int<lower=2> K;
  int<lower=2> V;
  int<lower=1> M;
  int<lower=1> N; 
  int<lower=1> S;
  int<lower=1,upper=V> w[N];
  int<lower=1,upper=M> word_doc[N];
  vector[S] epu_mu;
  simplex[K] zeta0[S];
  simplex[V] xi0[K];
}
parameters {
  vector[K] Alpha[S];
  vector[V] Beta[K];
  vector[K] Eta[M,S];
  vector[S] Epu;
  vector[S] Epu2[M];
}
transformed parameters {
  simplex[K] Theta[M,S];
  simplex[V] PHi[K];
  simplex[S] Mu[M];
 
  for (m in 1:M){
    Mu[m] = softmax(Epu2[m]);
    for(s in 1:S){
    Theta[m,s] = softmax(Eta[m,s]);
  }
}
    for (k in 1:K) {
      PHi[k] = softmax(Beta[k]);
    }
  }
model {
  for(s in 1:S){
  Alpha[s] ~ normal(0,1);
}
  for (k in 1:K) {
      Beta[k] ~ normal(xi0[k],1);
    }
    Epu ~ normal(epu_mu,1);
  for (m in 1:M) {
    Epu2[m] ~ normal(Epu,1);
    for (s in 1:S) {
      Eta[m,s] ~ normal(Alpha[s] .* zeta0[s],1);
    }
  }
 
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real gamma2[S];
    for (s in 1:S) {
      real gamma1[K];
      for (k in 1:K)
      gamma1[k] = log(Theta[word_doc[n],s,k]) + log(PHi[k,w[n]]);
      gamma2[s] = log(Mu[word_doc[n],s]) + log_sum_exp(gamma1);
    }
    target += log_sum_exp(gamma2);
}
}

Thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to speed up my stan code.
parts:
Sorry--- missed this before. YOU want to avoid recomputing
shared subexpressions (such as log(Mu), log(Theta), log(Mu)
to be saved in log_Mu, log_Theta, and log_Mu and then be
used in vectorized form in the expressions).

For example,

can be

gamma1 = log_Theta[word_doc, s] + log_Phi[ , w];

And vectorize the densities wherever you can.

Otherwise, Stan's not going to be fast at these kinds
of models, and to boot, you won't be able to do full Bayes
on them anyway because they're combinatorially intractable.

- Bob
